title: Microsoft Entra ID: passkey sign-in to Microsoft apps on Android through Authenticator or Company Portal
summary: The broker requirements, Android minimum versions, licensing, admin paths and Graph calls are supported. The assurances that user eligibility and application data access remain unchanged lack explicit supporting text and should be narrowed; the documented policy controls themselves check out.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Entra ID passkey sign-in to Microsoft apps on Android with Microsoft Authenticator or Intune Company Portal installed as a broker.
claims.quote: Microsoft Entra ID users can now use a passkey to sign into Microsoft apps on Android devices where an authentication broker like Microsoft Authenticator or Microsoft Intune Company Portal is installed.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The Passkey (FIDO2) policy governs which targeted users can register and sign in with Entra ID passkeys.

claims.claim: Nothing about who may use passkeys changes.

claims.fix: Remove 'Nothing about who may use passkeys changes.' Keep the following sentence about users needing to be allowed by the Passkey (FIDO2) policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Passkeys provide phishing-resistant authentication.
claims.quote: Passkeys are FIDO2-based credentials that provide strong, phishing-resistant authentication.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Passkeys in Authenticator are device-bound.
claims.quote: Passkeys in the Authenticator app are device-bound to ensure that they never leave the device they were created on.

claims.claim: Authenticator creates Android passkeys in the Secure Element on devices that support it.
claims.quote: On Android, we create the passkey in the Secure Element on devices that support it, or fall back to the Trusted Execution Environment (TEE).

claims.claim: Authenticator otherwise creates Android passkeys in the Trusted Execution Environment.
claims.quote: On Android, we create the passkey in the Secure Element on devices that support it, or fall back to the Trusted Execution Environment (TEE).

claims.claim: Synced passkeys, including Google Password Manager passkeys, are stored with a cloud passkey provider.
claims.quote: This encrypted key is then synced and stored in the cloud passkey provider. Other devices authenticated with the passkey provider may then use the passkey. This may differ depending on the provider.

claims.claim: Synced passkeys do not support attestation.
claims.quote: Synced passkeys do not support attestation.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises treating synced passkeys as having the same security posture as other unattested authenticators.
claims.quote: Treat synced passkeys as phishing-resistant credentials but with the same security posture as other unattested authenticators.

claims.claim: Passkey profiles provide group-based passkey type and authenticator-provider controls.
claims.quote: Passkey profiles enable granular group-based configurations for passkey (FIDO2) authentication. Instead of a single tenant-wide setting, you can define specific requirements such as attestation, passkey type (device-bound or synced), or Authenticator Attestation GUID (AAGUID) restrictions.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no licensing requirement specific to the Android passkey broker scenario.

Read passkey enablement, Authenticator overview and MSAL broker excerpts; no broker-specific SKU.

Read passkey enablement and Authenticator overview; no passkey meter found.

claims.claim: Using Company Portal as the Android broker ties into an Intune deployment.
claims.quote: On Android, Microsoft Intune establishes the managed context that passwordless and brokered authentication flows depend on. This context is especially relevant when Microsoft Authenticator or related app experiences are part of your mobile access design.
claims.fix: Remove 'Using Company Portal as the broker ties into an Intune deployment, but' and retain 'Microsoft publishes no licence requirement specific to this broker scenario.' This avoids implying that using the broker necessarily requires an Intune deployment, and avoids relying on an uncited background page.

claims.claim: Registration of Entra passkeys is not supported for internal or external guest users.
claims.quote: Registration of passkey (FIDO2) credentials isn't supported for internal or external guest users, including B2B collaboration users in the resource tenant.

claims.claim: At least Authentication Policy Administrator is needed to configure passkey profiles and targets.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Authentication Policy Administrator.

claims.claim: At least Conditional Access Administrator is needed to create a custom authentication strength.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Conditional Access Administrator.

claims.claim: The Entra admin center route through Security, Authentication methods, Policies, Passkey (FIDO2), Enable and Target, Add target, a target and passkey profiles configures group targeting and profile assignment.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies. Select Passkey (FIDO2). Select Enable and Target. Select Add target, and then choose All users or Select targets to choose specific groups. Select the passkey profiles that you want to assign to a specific target.

claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies. Select Passkey (FIDO2). On the Configure tab, select + Add passkey profile. Fill in the profile details.
claims.fix: For the passkey-type control, extend the UI path to 'Entra ID > Security > Authentication methods > Policies > Passkey (FIDO2) > Configure > + Add passkey profile > Passkey types'. Keep the note naming Enforce attestation and Enforce key restrictions as other settings in that form.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: An authentication strength is enforced when a Conditional Access policy uses it as a grant control.
claims.quote: When a conditional access policy applies to a sign-in and that policy has an authentication strength grant control, the user will be required to use one of the allowed authentication method combinations to sign in.

claims.claim: No separate UI or API switch is documented for Entra-issued passkey sign-in in brokered Microsoft apps on Android.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Entra brokered Android passkey authentication separate setting authentication methods policy enable disable. Read matrix, passkey enablement, FIDO2 Graph update and federated-browser page; systemBrowserEnabledOn concerns external IdP browser handoff, not Entra-issued passkeys.
claims.fix: Replace 'There is no separate switch for passkey sign-in in brokered Android apps' with 'Microsoft Learn documents no separate switch for Entra-issued passkey sign-in in brokered Android apps at the time of writing (November 2026)'. Keep the following statement that the Passkey (FIDO2) policy governs Entra passkeys.

claims.claim: Users in excluded groups are blocked from FIDO2 passkey registration and sign-in entirely.
claims.quote: If a user is a member of an excluded group in the Passkeys (FIDO2) authentication method policy, they're blocked from FIDO2 passkey registration or sign-in entirely

claims.claim: Passkey policy exclusion takes precedence over membership in an included group.
claims.quote: and this takes precedence over them being in any Included groups.

claims.claim: After opting in to passkey profiles, administrators cannot opt out.
claims.quote: After you opt in to enable passkey profiles, you can't opt out.

claims.claim: Removing a previously allowed AAGUID from enforced key restrictions prevents users with that registered method from signing in with it.
claims.quote: Key restrictions set the usability of specific models or providers for both registration and authentication. If you change key restrictions and remove an AAGUID that you previously allowed, users who previously registered an allowed method can no longer use it for sign-in.

claims.claim: Enforce attestation is a passkey-profile setting.
claims.quote: A passkey profile is a named set of policy rules that governs how users in targeted groups can register and authenticate with passkeys (FIDO2). Profiles support advanced controls such as: | Enforce attestation | Enabled, Disabled |

claims.claim: Enforce key restrictions allows or disallows providers identified by AAGUID within a passkey profile.
claims.quote: Enforce key restrictions should be set to Yes only if your organization wants to only allow or disallow certain security key models or passkey providers, which are identified by their AAGUID.

claims.claim: The described passkey sign-in flow is initiated by the user rather than taking action on its own.
claims.quote: If a user installed an authentication broker, they can choose to sign in with a passkey when they access an app such as Outlook. They're redirected to sign in with passkey, and redirected back to Outlook as a signed in user after successful authentication.
